docs.title: rdfnav.GraphNavigator dataclass
docs.text:
Wraps an RDF graph and provides methods to navigate through it using URIs.

Attributes:

Name Type Description graph str

The RDFLib graph to navigate

docs.title: graph: Graph instance-attribute
docs.text: The RDFLib graph to navigate

docs.title: __getitem__(uri: IdentifiedNode) -> UriNode
docs.text: Traverses to a given node

docs.title: ask_query(query: str, **kwargs: Any) -> bool
docs.text:
Executes a SPARQL ASK query on the graph. Returns True if the query returns any results, False otherwise.

This is a type-safe version of the query method that expects an ASK query.

docs.title: construct_query(query: str, **kwargs: Any) -> Graph
docs.text:
Executes a SPARQL CONSTRUCT query on the graph. Returns a subgraph containing the results of the query.

This is a type-safe version of the query method that expects a CONSTRUCT query.

docs.title: describe_query(query: str, **kwargs: Any) -> Graph
docs.text:
Executes a SPARQL DESCRIBE query on the graph. Returns a subgraph containing the results of the query.

This is a type-safe version of the query method that expects a DESCRIBE query.

docs.title: instance(type_uri: Subject) -> UriNode
docs.text: Returns a single navigator object for an instance of the given type URI.

docs.title: instances(type_uri: Subject) -> Iterable[UriNode]
docs.text: Yields navigator objects for all instances of the given type URI.

docs.title: select_query(query: str, **kwargs: Any) -> Iterable[ResultRow]
docs.text:
Executes a SPARQL SELECT query on the graph. Returns an iterable of tuples containing the results of the query.

This is a type-safe version of the query method that expects a SELECT query.

docs.title: subject(predicate: URIRef, object: URIRef) -> UriNode
docs.text: Yields a single navigator object for the subject of the given predicate and object. Raises an error if there are is not exactly one such subject.

docs.title: subjects(predicate: Predicate, object: Object) -> Iterable[UriNode]
docs.text: Yields navigator objects for all nodes that are subjects of the given predicate and object

docs.title: rdfnav.UriNode dataclass
docs.text:
Navigation helper for a single node in the RDF graph, identified by a URI. Typically this is created by the GraphNavigator class.

Attributes:

Name Type Description navigator str

Navigator for the parent graph

iri str

The current location in the graph, as an RDFLib identifier

docs.title: graph: Graph property
docs.text: Returns the graph that this node belongs to.

docs.title: iri: IdentifiedNode instance-attribute
docs.text: The current location in the graph, as an RDFLib identifier

docs.title: navigator: GraphNavigator instance-attribute
docs.text: Navigator for the parent graph

docs.title: suffix: str property
docs.text: Returns the suffix of the URI, which is the last part after the last slash or hash.

docs.title: add(predicate: _PredicateType, obj: _ObjectType) -> Self
docs.text: Adds a new triple with the current IRI as subject, the given predicate and object. This mutates the graph.

docs.title: ask_query(query: str, binding: str = 'node', **kwargs: Any) -> bool
docs.text:
Executes a SPARQL ASK query on the graph, with the current node pre-bound into the graph.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default query str

The SPARQL query to execute.

required binding str

The variable name to bind the current node to in the query. Defaults to "node".

'node'

docs.title: cbd() -> Graph
docs.text: Returns the Concise Bounded Description (CBD) of the current node

docs.title: change_iri(new_iri: Subject) -> Self
docs.text: Changes all instance of the current IRI to a new IRI. This mutates the graph.

docs.title: construct_query(query: str, binding: str = 'node', **kwargs: Any) -> Graph
docs.text:
Executes a SPARQL CONSTRUCT query on the graph, with the current node pre-bound into the graph.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default query str

The SPARQL query to execute.

required binding str

The variable name to bind the current node to in the query. Defaults to "node".

'node'

docs.title: delete(pred: _PredicateType, obj: _ObjectType | None = None) -> Self
docs.text: Deletes all triples that have the current IRI as subject and the given predicate and optionally object. This mutates the graph.

docs.title: describe_query(query: str, binding: str = 'node', **kwargs: Any) -> Graph
docs.text:
Executes a SPARQL DESCRIBE query on the graph, with the current node pre-bound into the graph.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default query str

The SPARQL query to execute.

required binding str

The variable name to bind the current node to in the query. Defaults to "node".

'node'

docs.title: is_instance_of(type_uri: IdentifiedNode) -> bool
docs.text: Checks if the current node is a subclass of the given type URI.

docs.title: is_subclass_of(type_uri: IdentifiedNode) -> bool
docs.text: Checks if the current node is a subclass of the given type URI.

docs.title: lit_obj_via(predicate: Predicate) -> Any
docs.text: Returns one literal that can be reached from the current object using predicate. Fails if there are no objects or more than one object.

docs.title: lit_objs() -> Iterable[tuple[URIRef, Any]]
docs.text: Yields pair of predicates and literal objects that can be reached from the current object.

docs.title: lit_objs_prefix(*prefixes: str) -> Iterable[tuple[URIRef, Any]]
docs.text: Yields tuples of (predicate, literal) for objects that can be reached from the current object using predicates that start with prefix.

docs.title: lit_objs_sans_prefix(*prefixes: str) -> Iterable[tuple[str, Any]]
docs.text: Yields tuples of (predicate without prefix, literal) for all objects that can be reached from the current object.

docs.title: lit_objs_via(predicate: Predicate) -> Iterable[Any]
docs.text: Yields all literals that can be reached from the current object using predicate.

docs.title: ref_obj_via(predicate: Predicate) -> UriNode
docs.text: Yields one UriNode that can be reached from the current object using predicate. Fails if there are no objects or more than one object.

docs.title: ref_objs() -> Iterable[tuple[Predicate, UriNode]]
docs.text: Yields pairs of predicates and object nodes that can be reached from the current object. Only predicates that are URIs are included, literals are excluded.

docs.title: ref_objs_prefix(*prefixes: str) -> Iterable[tuple[URIRef, UriNode]]
docs.text: Yields tuples of (predicate, UriNode) for objects that can be reached from the current object using predicates that start with prefix.

docs.title: ref_objs_sans_prefix(*prefixes: str) -> Iterable[tuple[str, UriNode]]
docs.text: Yields tuples of (predicate without prefix, UriNode) for all objects that can be reached from the current object,

docs.title: ref_objs_via(predicate: Predicate | None = None) -> Iterable[UriNode]
docs.text:
Yields navigator objects for all nodes that can be reached from the current object using predicate.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default predicate Predicate | None

Optionally, a specific predicate to follow to find subjects. If None, all objects that are URIs or BNodes that can be reached from the current object will be returned.

None

docs.title: ref_subj_via(predicate: Predicate) -> UriNode
docs.text: Yields one UriNode that can reach the current object using predicate. Fails if there are no subjects or more than one subject.

docs.title: ref_subjs() -> Iterable[UriNode]
docs.text: Yields all subjects that can reach the current object via one predicate, as UriNode instances.

docs.title: ref_subjs_via(predicate: Predicate) -> Iterable[UriNode]
docs.text:
Yields all URIs that can reach the current object using predicate, as UriNode instances.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default predicate Predicate

Optionally, a specific predicate to follow to find subjects. If None, all subjects of the current object will be returned.

required

docs.title: replace(predicate: _PredicateType, obj: _ObjectType) -> Self
docs.text: Replaces all triples with the current IRI as subject and the given predicate with a new object. This mutates the graph.

docs.title: select_query(query: str, binding: str = 'node', **kwargs: Any) -> Iterable[ResultRow]
docs.text:
Executes a SPARQL SELECT query on the graph, with the current node pre-bound into the graph.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default query str

The SPARQL query to execute.

required binding str

The variable name to bind the current node to in the query. Defaults to "node".

'node'

docs.title: subgraph() -> Graph
docs.text: Returns a subgraph containing only the current node and anything traversable from it.
